title: The model and its runtime
intro: A model can propose a tool call. The surrounding software prepares inputs, checks permissions, executes the call and supplies results. That surrounding setup is part of the harness.
takeaway: Instructions express what should happen; executable software decides what actually runs.

beats.text: The model proposes a tool call. It does not execute the tool by itself.
The runtime receives the request. It checks and dispatches the operation.
The tool runs and produces a result. The runtime captures that evidence.
The model receives the captured result. The harness connects action to feedback.

title: Prepare a known workspace
intro: A long-running task needs a known starting state. The harness prepares the repository, instructions and a way to run relevant checks before work begins.
takeaway: Reproducible setup reduces ambiguity. It does not make every task deterministic or guarantee the environment is correct.

beats.text: Begin with a known repository revision. Setup prepares the working directory.
Load the task and repository instructions. They define the work and its boundaries.
Run a baseline check before editing. Record existing failures separately.
The starting evidence is now recorded. Later results can be compared with it.

title: Execute and retain evidence
intro: The agent requests a test. The harness runs the actual command and retains the exit status and output for later inspection.
takeaway: A statement that tests passed is different from a recorded command and its result. Bind evidence to the code that was tested.

beats.text: The agent asks to run the tests. A test runner executes the command.
Capture the exit status and output. Do not replace them with a success claim.
Associate evidence with the code revision. A new patch needs new evidence.
Return that evidence to the agent. Its next decision uses an observation.

title: Turn a failure into feedback
intro: An invoice endpoint should deny cross-tenant access under this example contract. A failed authorization test supplies a concrete expected-versus-actual result.
takeaway: Useful feedback names the violated behavior. The harness must rerun the relevant checks against the repair.

beats.text: This example denies cross-tenant access. Expected: 403. Actual: 200.
Return the failed assertion to the agent. The failure identifies what to repair.
The agent changes the authorization check. A proposed repair is not yet verified.
Rerun the access test on the patch. Now it returns the expected 403.

title: Require a passing check
intro: A mechanically enforced gate can prevent an unchecked change from advancing. The gate needs a relevant check, current evidence and controlled bypass permissions.
takeaway: A prompt asking for tests is not a required-check mechanism. Passing checks cover only their tested behavior.

beats.text: The patch is ready for evaluation. The merge path still blocks it.
A required check runs on this revision. The gate waits for its actual result.
The configured checks pass. The gate records current evidence.
This gate now permits advancement. Other review requirements still apply.
